h1: Sponsoring gigs, quizzes and sports nights as a small brewery
title: Sponsoring Gigs, Quizzes and Sports | Craft Beer School
desc: How a small brewery can sponsor gigs, quiz nights and sports screenings well: choosing events, structuring the deal and measuring the return.
teaser: A banner at a gig nobody remembers is money gone. A quiz round named after your stout that people talk about next week is marketing.
standfirst: Sponsoring local events is one of the oldest ways for a brewery to get known. It is also one of the easiest to waste money on. We look at how a small brewery can pick events that fit, structure deals sensibly and tell whether they worked.
sections:
Craft beer is a local, social product. People try a new beer when a friend hands them one at an event they enjoy. Sponsorship puts your beer in exactly that moment. It also suits Indian conditions, where alcohol advertising is restricted and brands have to build presence through experience rather than mass media.

It is also cheap compared with most marketing. A keg, a few vouchers and an evening of a staff member's time can put your beer in front of eighty new people who are already in a good mood.

For a small brewery, the best sponsorships are not big festivals with dozens of logos. They are regular, smaller events where your brewery is the main or only partner and people return week after week.

Quiz nights. Bengaluru, Pune, Kolkata and other cities have lively quiz scenes with loyal crowds. A regular quiz is a weekly audience of curious, social people who sit for two hours. A round themed on beer or your brewery is memorable without being pushy.

Gigs. Independent music nights draw people who like discovering things, a good match for craft beer. Small venues and regular nights work better than one-off big shows.

Sports nights. Cricket, football and Formula 1 screenings pull groups who stay for hours. Note that screening matches commercially can need permission from the rights holder, so check this with the venue.

Ask three questions of any event: do its audience look like your drinkers, will they remember you and can you be there regularly?

Sponsorship need not be cash. Common structures for small breweries include:

  • Beer in kind. A keg or set number of pours for prizes or the hosts.
  • Prize vouchers. Winners get a voucher redeemable at your taproom, which brings them to you.
  • A named element. A quiz round, a weekly gig slot or a man of the match award carrying your brewery or beer name.
  • Exclusive pour. Your beer is the featured tap for the event at the host venue.

Write down what each side gives and gets, how often and for how long. Agree how your name and logo appear and who approves posts. A short agreement avoids awkward conversations later.
Keep it responsible and within the rules

Alcohol promotion in India is tightly controlled and rules vary by state. Showing alcohol brand names at events, on banners and in social posts can fall under advertising restrictions. Many breweries use their brewery or taproom name rather than beer names, or focus on the experience. Our guide to alcohol advertising rules explains the background. A licensing adviser can help with specifics.

Keep prizes moderate. A voucher for a tasting flight is better than "a free pitcher for every right answer". Never sponsor events aimed at students or anyone under the legal drinking age. Make sure there are good non-alcoholic options and that hosts encourage getting home safely.
Being present, not just a logo

The difference between a sponsorship that works and one that does not is usually presence. Send someone from the brewery: a brewer to say a few words about the beer, a staff member to run a quick tasting of small pours, someone to chat with guests. A person is remembered. A banner is not.

Pair the event with your own taproom events. If the quiz winners get a voucher, invite them to a brewery tour or a new beer launch. That turns a one-night audience into regulars.

Small breweries rarely measure sponsorship, so they cannot tell good deals from bad ones. Simple measures:

  • Count how many prize vouchers were redeemed at the taproom.
  • Ask new customers how they heard about you and note event mentions.
  • Track follows and mentions on social media in the days after each event.
  • Compare sales of your beer at the host venue on event nights against other nights.

After three months, compare the cost of beer, staff time and vouchers against what came back. Keep the events that brought people through your door and drop the ones that only produced a photo.

Sponsorship works best as part of a wider plan for building a beer community, where each event feeds into the next.
faqs: What events should a small brewery sponsor?
Regular local events whose audience matches your drinkers, such as quiz nights, independent gigs and sports screenings, where you can be the main partner.
Does sponsorship have to be cash?
No. Beer in kind, prize vouchers, named rounds and exclusive pours are common and often more effective for small breweries.
Can a brewery put its beer name on event banners in India?
Alcohol promotion is restricted and rules vary by state. Check current rules with a licensing adviser before using beer names in event branding.
